blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — At least 10 countries and the European Union have thrown their support behind the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC), urging the Philippine government to cut bureaucratic red tape, streamline investment approvals and provide clearer business rules to turn foreign investment commitments into actual projects. Led by United States Ambassador Lee Lipton, the diplomatic representatives said the success of the corridor would depend not only on international partnerships and financing but also on the government’s ability to make it easier for companies to do business in the Philippines.
